title: Add fishing from the beaches as year-round food
body:
- New tech Fishing (after Gathering); SIM_VERSION 2 marks shore tiles and stocks 240 fish
- Idle adults fish from beach sand: 3-6 food per 4h trip, all year incl. winter
- Fish regrow 5/day (2/day in winter); live world catches ~1700 food/yr at 13 people
- Fishers show in teal with a rod and bobbing line; "+n" catches pop in teal
- Watch: winter shore activity, and whether spring stores rise in the early years

title: Add granaries; grain left in the open now rots
body:
- New tech Granaries (after Farming + Woodcutting); SIM_VERSION 3 tags old buildings as houses
- Each house keeps 150 food dry, each granary 2500; dry food spoils 0.05%/day, the rest 0.2%/day
- Villagers raise a granary (30 timber, 24h) when stores pass 85% of dry space, up to 1 per 12 people
- Long-run stores drop from ~900 days of food to ~150-300; panel shows granaries and grain rotting
- Watch: the first granary on Hais this spring, and whether births slow when stores dip below 250/person

title: Add daily weather: rain, storms, heatwaves, frost, snow
body:
- SIM_VERSION 4: each day's weather is a seasonal Markov chain (clear, rain, storm, heat, cold snap, snow), so bad days come in runs
- Rain speeds crop growth x1.25, heat slows it to x0.4, cold to x0.5; cold snaps double winter firewood and chill the frail; heat is hard on elders
- Storms keep everyone indoors, flatten 3% of tall fields per day and can tear off a roof (repaired as a building job)
- Visible: rain, snow, storm flashes, heat haze, tinted sky, snow on roofs, roofless houses, flattened fields; weather shown next to the date
- Watch: slower early growth (100-yr pop ~260 vs ~280), and woods lasting longer (forest ~450 tiles at Y100 vs ~210)

title: Add wolves and boars to the woods of the island
body:
- SIM_VERSION 5: a wolf pack dens in the deepest forest, boars lie up in cover near the fields (3 each, herd size follows forest cover)
- Wolves prowl the treeline from dusk to dawn (and on winter cold snaps); a lone adult away from the houses can be bitten (12 days laid up) or killed; a helper nearby drives the wolf off. ~1 attack and ~0.1 deaths a year
- After an attack the village comes in at 16:00 and goes out at 07:00 for 45 days; boars root through growing grain near the woods on ~14 spring/summer nights a year
- Visible: grey wolves with glowing eyes at night, boars rooting in fields, torn-up field tiles, bandaged villagers, a Wilds row in the panel
- Watch: first bite and first raid in the chronicle; 100-yr pop ~217 vs ~259 before

title: Add hunting: boar and wolf hunts, meat and hides
body:
- New tech Hunting (SIM_VERSION 6); live world learns it on load, new worlds after the first boar raid or wolf attack
- Every 6 days a pair sets out at dawn for the boar lair, or the wolf den in winter and after an attack; trip must fit before dusk
- Success 50% boar / 35% wolf (about half alone); 8-10% chance the beast turns, rarely fatal; herds never hunted below 2
- Kills are carried home on a shoulder (+45 meat boar, +12 wolf); hides dry on a rack by the hearth, cut winter firewood up to 30%, wear out yearly
- Visible: red hunters with spears, carcass on the way home, hide rack, Hunt row in panel; watch for the first boar taken on Hais this spring

title: Speed up the simulation about 4x with identical results
body:
- Cache the best field site until a tile changes; keep a daily list of tall trees near the hearth
- Find the nearest fishing spot by 8x8 map blocks; index houses by id; per-hour lists of ripe/fallow fields and unfinished buildings
- Same world, same choices: fingerprints match the old code for 100 years on seed 4242 and 15 years on the live world
- Seed 4242: 2773 -> 631 ms per year on average, ~1.5 s at 331 people (was ~8 s); browsers catch up faster on load
- Watch: tiles must now change through setTile() in the step path, or the field-site cache goes stale

title: Add wattle fences to keep boars out of the fields
body:
- New tech Fences (SIM_VERSION 7), learned after the 8th boar raid; the live world (2 raids so far) should learn it in early summer of Y1
- Idle workers fence fields within 2 tiles of the woods (3 timber, 3 h, not in winter); a fence turns a boar away for the night 85% of the time
- Fences wear out: 20% rot each new year, 2% per storm day blow down, and a boar that gets through breaks the fence, so mending never ends
- Raid nights drop from ~10 to ~3.5 a year; fences drawn as woven hazel edges with stakes around each fenced block; Fields row shows how many are fenced
- Watch: the first fence and the first night the boars are turned away in the chronicle

title: Add a midsummer festival with bonfire and ring dance
body:
- New custom Midsummer (SIM_VERSION 8, w.fest); the live world learns it on load, new worlds at 10 people
- On summer day 46 work stops at 16:00: everyone gathers at a big bonfire (up to 12 timber), feasts 2 food each if stores allow, and dances until 23:00; rain delays it up to 4 days, a storm until it clears
- At 21:00 each single woman has a 40% chance to pair up in the firelight; the year's festival is logged, the 1st and every 25th go in the chronicle
- Visible: tall flickering bonfire with rising sparks, villagers in rings turning around it with flower crowns, "midsummer fire" next to the date
- Watch: the first midsummer on Hais this summer (Y1, about 70 game days away)

title: Add click-to-follow: a life card for any islander
body:
- Click a villager to follow them: the camera glides to them and keeps them centred, with thin white brackets around them (dashed round their house while they sleep)
- A card shows name, age, what they are doing, parents, partner, children and housemates; click any name to follow that person instead
- The card also lists the last three log entries that mention them; if they die it says so and shows how
- Drag to look around (the card stays, "find" brings the camera back); click empty ground, press Esc or the cross to let go
- Render only: no change to the simulation, saved state or SIM_VERSION

title: Add fever outbreaks that spread through crowded houses
body:
- SIM_VERSION 9 (w.fever, p.sick, p.imm): a fever can take hold any day, most often in autumn and winter, more in crowded houses and bigger villages; castaways bring it ashore 15% of the time
- It spreads 10%/day per sick housemate plus a little across the village; 6-10 days in bed, then 4 years immune, so outbreaks burn out
- Sick islanders stop working and skip midsummer; infants and elders are most at risk (~3-4% of cases die, double when hungry or cold); 100-yr pop on seed 20261114 drops ~199 -> 151
- Visible: sick lie under a blanket in their doorway, pale green "fever" pops, "n sick" on the People row, "laid up with fever" on the follow card
- Watch: the first fever on Hais (likely within the first in-world year or two); outbreak ends are logged, and ones that take 3+ lives go in the chronicle

title: Add footpaths worn into the grass by daily walking
body:
- SIM_VERSION 10 (w.wear per tile): each hour's walk wears the grass it crosses; grass heals 1/day spring to autumn, not under snow
- Tiles worn to 24+ become bare-earth paths: walking on them is 4 tiles/h instead of 3, and the woods cannot regrow over them
- New tech Footpaths is noticed in-world once a track of 12+ path tiles leads 7+ tiles out from the hearth (the live world should see it within weeks of game time)
- Visible: scuffed grass, then ragged dirt tracks that join houses, beach and fields (grey slush in winter); Paths row in the panel
- Watch: trails to the beach and woodlots stay open as forest closes in; ~90-120 path tiles on test seeds

title: Add a burying ground where families mourn their dead
body:
- SIM_VERSION 11 (w.graves, w.yard, p.mourn): the first death walls off a 4x3 plot 6-14 tiles from the hearth; new custom Burying ground is logged in the chronicle
- Each grave keeps name, age, cause and parents; 50 places in rows, after which the oldest stone sinks and its place is reused
- The morning after a death, partner, parents, children, siblings and housemates stand at the graveside 9:00-12:00 (shown in grey-blue)
- Visible: dry-stone wall with a gate toward the village, fresh mounds with a stake and flowers, grassed graves with stones; hover a grave for who lies there; Graves row in the panel
- Fix build: export every sim constant to the page, so footpaths (PATH_AT, WEAR_SEEN) now actually draw in the browser

title: Add a deer herd that grazes the open meadow by day
body:
- SIM_VERSION 12: four deer join the beasts (k 'deer'); they feed on the widest grass 9+ tiles from the hearth (fauna.mead) from 05:00 to 21:00 and lie up in nearby trees (fauna.bed) at night
- Deer bolt when a grown islander comes within ~3.5 tiles, and nibble saplings (wood <= 3) back to grass, so their meadow stays open
- Herd size follows open grass (1 deer per 45 tiles, 2-8); fawns in spring, one leaves in autumn if the meadow has shrunk; wolves take ~1 in winter and then lie up for two days
- Hunters stalk deer in autumn only (2 a year, never below 3): +30 meat and a hide; panel, tooltip and follow card show deer
- Watch: the first venison on Hais this autumn, and the herd thinning as fields eat the grass in later decades

title: Add surf, chimney smoke and gulls to the map
body:
- Waves run up to every beach and draw back; rain and storms push the foam wider and faster, with spray in storms
- Lived-in houses smoke: all day in winter and on cold or snowy days, mornings and evenings in spring and autumn, only at supper in summer; storms flatten the smoke sideways
- Gulls wheel over the shallows by day and drift over to whoever is fishing; fewer in winter, none at night or in storms
- Render only: no change to the simulation, saved state or SIM_VERSION
- Watch: the first winter on Hais, when every roof should be smoking

title: Add sea fog: wolves hunt by day in the grey
body:
- SIM_VERSION 13: new weather kind 'fog' (spring 7%, summer 3%, autumn 10%, winter 5% of new spells; holds 55%); crops grow at 0.8x
- In fog nobody fishes or sets out to hunt, walking off a path drops to 2 tiles/h (paths stay 4), and wolves leave the trees by day at half their dusk boldness
- First fog bank is a chronicle milestone; spells of 4+ days or with a wolf attack are logged, wolf kills in fog go in the chronicle; yearly history gets `fog` days
- Visible: grey wash, slow drifting fog banks over the map, flat faint surf, no gulls, sea glints hidden; "sea fog" in pale grey next to the date
- Watch: the live world's first fog (spring/autumn most likely) and a daytime wolf attack; test seeds see ~1 fog death per 20-30 years

title: Add herb lore and a village healer
body:
- SIM_VERSION 14 (w.heal, p.tend): new tech Herb lore, learned after the first fever death or 8 fever cases; one islander becomes the healer
- The healer tends each sick or bitten islander once a day (1 herb bundle): a tended fever is half as deadly, each tending takes 2 days off a wound
- Herbs are gathered at the wood's edge spring to autumn (cap 30, 40% crumble each new year), so a long winter outbreak can run the bundles dry
- The basket passes to the healer's child, a housemate, or a woman of ~28 when the healer dies or turns 62; each new healer goes in the chronicle
- Visible: green healer with a basket, herb bundles under the healer's eaves, a Herbs row in the panel, "herb-woman" on the follow card. Watch for the first fever on Hais (test seeds learn herb lore around Y5-6)

title: Show dates in the sky and a list of changes
body:
- Each star shows the game date it was learned
- Hover a star to see the real date it was added
- New panel in the sky lists every change with its date

title: Add a History view with one entry per island year
body:
- New History button opens a timeline of every island year, newest first
- Each year shows its real date, people, births, deaths, harvest and main events
- Population chart over the whole life of the island

title: Add rats that breed in the grain heaps and stores
body:
- SIM_VERSION 16 (w.rats): from year 2, rats find grain heaped in the open (500+) or a large store (4000+)
- They breed fast while grain lies outside, slowly when all is under a roof, and die back in a winter with nothing left out
- Colony capped at 30 + 15 per granary (max 150, never above food/80); each rat eats 0.05 grain a day, and a swarm makes fevers up to 60% likelier
- Visible: rats run around the granaries, many at night, with spilled grain under a swarmed store; a Rats row in the panel; rats in History
- Watch: Hais has ~3000 grain in the open, so rats should arrive within weeks; nobody has an answer to them yet

title: Add goats: a raft brings a herd, a pen and a goatherd
body:
- SIM_VERSION 17 (w.goats): some spring or summer day a raft drifts ashore with three goats; a 2x2 wattle pen goes up 5-12 tiles from the hearth and the new Goats tech is logged in the chronicle
- A child of 7-13 (the eldest adult if none) takes the crook and walks the herd to fresh grass every few hours, 07:00-16:00; the herd stays in on storm, snow and winter cold days
- Goats eat back saplings near the pen, give milk in spring and summer (0.8 a day each), eat 1.5 spare grain each per winter day, kid in spring, and in autumn the old and any the grass can't carry are killed for meat and hides (herd 3-14)
- Unminded goats get into unfenced young grain; in fog a wolf may take a goat that strays from the herder (goatsLost in yearly history)
- Visible: pen with straw and a lean-to, white, brown and black goats that graze head-down, skipping kids, a herder's crook; hover tooltip, Goats panel row, goatherd tag on the life card

title: Add lost-in-the-fog searches with torches at night
body:
- SIM_VERSION 18 (w.lost): on a fog day a child of 3-10 or an islander over 72 can wander off 8-15 tiles from the hearth
- After 2 hours they are missed; every able adult goes searching in a ring that closes in, carrying torches through the night
- Lost children can be targeted by wolves, and a winter night out can kill; when the fog lifts they see the hearth smoke and walk home
- Visible: torches and their glow on searchers, a lost child sitting hunched, "X lost in the fog" in the People row, searches in History
- Watch: Hais gets ~20 fog days a year, so expect the first search within a few years; test seeds see ~25 per century

title: Add a fog horn blown at the hearth on fog days
body:
- SIM_VERSION 19 (w.horn, fauna.fa): the first fog morning after a wolf attack out of the fog (or a lost child) teaches the Fog horn tech
- On fog days 06:00-21:00, and all night during a search, the oldest able adult stands at the hearth and blows a whelk shell
- Within 13 tiles of the hearth nobody counts as alone in fog, so wolves pick only those working farther out; someone lost may follow the sound home
- Visible: keeper raises the shell, thin white sound rings roll out over the fog, Horn row in the panel, "blowing the fog horn" on the life card
- Watch: Hais already lost Saaris to fog wolves, so it learns the horn on its next fog morning; fog attacks deep in the woods still happen

title: Add a far isle whose boat comes to the midsummer fire
body:
- SIM_VERSION 20 (w.isle {n visits, wed, gone, hides, grain, boat}): from year 3, on midsummer day with a towering fire, a dugout with 2-4 guests may paddle in (50% the first time, 40% after); the first landing teaches the Far isle tech
- Guests wait by the hearth, dance in the outer ring, trade 1-3 hides for up to 300 spare grain, sleep by the embers and leave at first light
- A single islander with nobody to marry at home may be pledged to a guest, who stays (fixes Hais, where two single women have no match); once 30+ live there a lonely young islander may sail away with them, and 8% of visits leave a fever
- Visible: dugout with paddles and wake, sea-blue guests with a white feather, Far isle panel row, hover tips; also fix "A week of rain end" style lines
- Watch: Hais has timber for a towering fire, so a boat may come this midsummer (Y4 summer day 46)

title: Add hungry winter wolves that raid the goat pen
body:
- SIM_VERSION 21 (goats.pr/pk/yp/gap): on a winter night (2.5%, x2 in frost or snow, halved while 4+ deer remain) one wolf walks straight to the back wall of the goat pen, hearth or no hearth
- The wattle holds 35% of the time; otherwise someone asleep in a house within 6 tiles may run out with a brand (50%, 15% are bitten), or the youngest goat is dragged off
- No raids while the herd is under 3 goats; a torn wattle is mended next day for 2 timber
- Visible: a ragged hole and splayed rods in the pen's back wall, "wolves at the pen" and "wattle torn" in the Goats row, pen nights in History
- Watch: Hais has its first winter with goats this year; test seeds see ~3 pen nights and ~1 goat taken a winter, herds hold at 6-14

title: Add deeds and bynames: islanders earn names that stick
body:
- SIM_VERSION 22 (p.dd tally, w.by living holders, b.hands): each islander counts boars, wolves and deer taken, fish landed, grain reaped, roofs helped raise, lost ones found, wolves driven from the pen and sick tended; the migration counts in the hunts and finds still in the log
- Passing a mark (3 wolves, 10 kills, 2 finds, 10 roofs, 3,000 fish, 30,000 grain) gives a byname such as "the Wolf-slayer" or "the Fisher", told in the chronicle; only one living holder per name, it passes on at death
- A named islander's death is a chronicle entry that lists their life's deeds; graves keep the name and deeds
- Visible: byname in gold on the life card, hover tip and grave tip, a "so far" deeds line on the card, a Named row in the panel
- Watch: Vidor is 4 kills short of "the Hunter" and Duten 2 wolves short of "the Wolf-slayer"; test seeds see ~23 names per century

title: Add dogs: a wolf cub raised by the hearth
body:
- SIM_VERSION 23 (w.dogs {d [{id, nm, sex, b, own, x, y, lie}], n, k, f, p, r, dead}): from year 3, on a spring or summer day while the pack has 3+ wolves, a child may bring home a lone cub (1%/day); a second cub of the other sex follows, then a litter most springs up to pop/7 dogs (max 8)
- Each grown dog follows one islander (goatherd first, then the best hunter) and sleeps across their doorway; it flies at a wolf that springs on its owner (15% it dies doing it), barks the village awake at a pen raid (wake 90% instead of 50%), keeps wolves off nearby goats, scents lost ones in the fog within 7 tiles, catches a rat now and then, eats 0.5 grain a day, lives 10-14 years
- Visible: pixel dogs and pups at heel (tail wags when still, lie flat at night), hover tip, Dogs row in the panel, dog on the life card, dogs in History
- Watch: Hais is in year 4 spring with 3 wolves, so the first cub is likely this spring or summer; test seeds hold 1-8 dogs and can lose them all for a few years

title: Add the longest night: the eldest tells a winter tale
body:
- SIM_VERSION 24 (w.tale {y, on, n, id teller, told[], lore, k/j ring slots}; task kind 'tale'): from year 2, once there is a burying ground, on winter day 46 (put off by storm or snow until day 60) the village sits round the hearth from 18:00 to 23:00, children in an inner ring, and the eldest adult (30+) tells a tale at 21:00; the fire burns 4 extra timber
- Tales come from the island's own past and are not repeated while the 80 most recent are remembered: the fog, the landing, named dead and their deeds, the teller's own deeds, how living islanders got their bynames, the graves, and old chronicle entries; one chronicle entry per winter, tech 'tales' on the first
- The fog tale is a lesson: once told, children under 11 stay by the houses on 70% of fog hours when they would have strayed
- Visible: seated listeners in rings facing the fire, the teller standing on the far side with hands rising and falling, a higher fire and wider glow, "the longest night" in the top bar, a Tales row in the panel
- Watch: Hais holds its first tale night next winter (Y4 winter day 46); Morceem should tell the fog tale and name Saaris

title: Add night raids from the far isle in its thin years
body:
- SIM_VERSION 25 (w.raid {n, g, yg, d, lean, y, on, cur}; w.isle.feud): once the far isle has visited, each year has a 25% chance of being lean there (less with kin on both shores); in a lean year one autumn or early-winter night (3x likelier in fog) its dugout lands below the granary nearest the sea at 20:00
- 3-5 raiders creep up, force the door and carry off 70 grain each (at most 15% of the stores); each hour at the door someone in a nearby house may wake (15%, 45% with a dog by the granary, half in fog), and anyone still near the granary at first light is seen; the waker shouts the village awake, half the sacks are dropped, 25% chance the waker is knocked down (a wound)
- After a raid no boat comes to the next midsummer fire; when it returns "nobody speaks of the stolen grain"
- Visible: hooded raiders and sacks, islanders with brands chasing them to the beach, top-bar status, a Raiders row in the panel, raided grain in History
- Watch: the live world will most likely be raided in Y5 autumn, soon after the far isle's first visit; test seeds see about 5-12 raids per century, roughly half driven off

title: Add pottery: a potter, a kiln and jars rats can't open
body:
- SIM_VERSION 26 (w.pot {id, nm, k, kx/ky kiln, cx/cy clay bank, c clay, wet, sd, j jars, made, broke, f firings, lf}; tech 'pottery'; tasks 'clay', 'shape', 'fire'): once rats have eaten 1500 grain, someone (3%/day, spring to autumn) digs clay at the shore and builds a kiln 4-9 tiles from the hearth
- One potter (never the healer, herder or horn keeper; handed on at death or age 60) digs 3 lumps at the bank, coils one jar every other dry day and fires batches of 8 (6 timber, 25% crack); stops at min(60, food/100) jars; 12% of jars break each year
- Each jar seals 100 grain out of the rats' reach: the rat cap and what they eat now count only loose grain. On the live world rat losses drop from ~1000 a year to 0-800, and colonies now die out some winters and come back
- Visible: domed kiln with flames and smoke while firing (glow at dusk), grey hollows at the clay bank, pale jars drying by the kiln, red jars under the granary floors, potter colour and tooltips, a Jars row in the panel, jars in History
- Watch: Hais should learn it within weeks of island time (rats ate ~2600 grain already); expect ~45 jars in the first year

title: Add a beach watch fire that turns raiders back
body:
- SIM_VERSION 27 (w.watch {hid, last, x, y, n nights, s boats turned back, k turn}; tech 'watch'; task kind 'watch'): learned at the start of the raiding season once the far isle has raided twice
- From autumn to winter day 45, one adult (16-55, not herder, healer or horn keeper) in turn sits by a driftwood fire on the beach below the granary nearest the sea from 19:00 to 06:00 and sleeps until 11:00; costs 1 timber a night, skipped on storm, snow and tale nights; wolves leave the watcher alone
- A dugout rowing in is seen 80% of the time on a clear night (25% in fog, 50% in rain): it turns back with nothing and no feud follows, so the next midsummer boat still comes
- Visible: a small fire and glow on the beach at night, a hover tip for the watcher, a Watch row in the panel
- Watch: Hais (2 raids) learns it this autumn (Y7); test seeds learn it Y9-18 and turn back about one boat in 30 years

title: Add peace gifts: hungry guests go home with grain
body:
- SIM_VERSION 28 (w.raid.peace gifts, pg grain given, yv this year, gift year; tech 'gifts'; GIFT_* in sim.js; yearly `given`): in a thin year on the far isle its midsummer guests bring nothing to trade, and before the first raid they only eye the granaries
- Once raided, the islanders send each guest home with a 60-grain sack (at most 10% of the stores, 300 kept back per islander); that year no raid comes. The first gift is the tech milestone, told by the eldest
- Hungry years make the midsummer boat 1.5x likelier to come; a lean year with no visit, or the feud summer after a raid, can still bring raiders
- Visible: guests sleep beside and carry grain sacks to the dugout at first light, "at peace this year" and gift totals in the Raiders row, gifts in History
- Watch: Hais was raided twice and is in its feud summer; from Y8 a thin-year boat should bring the first gift. Test seeds: raids drop from 5-12 to 3-7 per century, 4-5 gifts

title: Add snowmen: children play in the winter snow
body:
- SIM_VERSION 29 (w.snow {k, n built ever, y this year, men [{id, x, y, s balls, m melting, nm, by}]}; tech 'snowmen'; task kind 'snow'; SNOW_* in sim.js; yearly `snowmen`): learned on the first winter snow day with two children aged 4-13
- On winter days without storm or fog, 2 of every 3 children go out to the green within 6 tiles of the hearth. They roll up to 3 snowmen (three balls each) and spend the rest of the day in snowball fights. Children do no work, so food and labour are unchanged
- Finished snowmen often get a name: someone living with a byname, a named grave, or the eldest. Each byname adds its own prop (spear, bracken pelt, torch, axe, straw crown). They melt ball by ball in spring, faster in rain and heat
- Visible: pixel snowmen with twig arms that lean and leave meltwater in spring, children patting snow and lobbing snowballs, hover tips, snowmen in History
- Watch: Hais learns it this coming winter (Y7) and builds 3 a winter, named after Vidor the Hunter and Duten the Wolf-slayer

title: Add summer wildfires that the village beats back
body:
- SIM_VERSION 30 (w.blaze; BLAZE_*/ASH_* in sim.js; task kind 'blaze'; yearly `burnt`): from Y2, a long heatwave or a dry storm after heat can set a tall tree alight
- Fire spreads tree to tree with a wind, through dry grass, standing grain and thatch; rain and night dew damp it. Every able adult goes out with green branches to the flames nearest the houses; beaten-out trees stand scorched, burnt ones turn to ash
- Burnt woods lie black for a season, then open grass with fireweed, then saplings; the woods refill in about 3 years
- Visible: flames and drifting smoke on burning tiles, a brown haze and night glow, beaters swinging branches, black ash, a Fire row, hover tips, History
- Watch: the live island should see a small first fire in summer Y8 and two 70-100 acre fires in Y10; test seeds get 20-40 fires a century, a few over 100 acres

title: Add a dugout canoe that fishes the deep water
body:
- SIM_VERSION 31 (w.canoe; CANOE_*/DEEP_* in sim.js; task kinds 'dig' and 'paddle'; tech 'canoe'; yearly `deep`): after two far-isle visits, the best fisher fells an oak (24 timber) above the landing beach and burns it hollow, one 4-hour spell per dry day (40 hours)
- On calm mornings from spring to autumn, one islander paddles out 2-7 tiles past the surf, fishes, and lands 12-21 fish by mid-afternoon. The deep water is a separate stock (220, +4 a day), so the shore fishers keep their shallows. Trips rank below chopping wood, so the boat never takes workers off the woodpile
- A storm can smash the boat on the beach (0.8% per storm day) and the wood can split at the new year (5%). Once there is timber to spare, another oak is felled
- Visible: a log with a smoking hollow while it is dug, the boat pulled up on the sand, the islander paddling with a wake or fishing over the side, a dog waiting on the beach, a Dugout row, tooltips, catch in History
- Watch: Hais should learn it in spring Y8 (Vidor) and land ~1,150 fish a year. Expect a lost boat every few years

title: Add hazel coppice stools that keep wood near the hearth
body:
- SIM_VERSION 32 (w.copse; COPSE_* in sim.js; tech 'coppice'; yearly `copse`): from spring Y8 the eldest notices shoots on an old stump and the 6 trees nearest the hearth are cut to the stool
- A tree within 14 tiles of the hearth that is chopped too small to fell again becomes a stool (up to 10 + 1.5 per house, max 150). Stools are cut all at once and grow back about 27 timber a year, against about 5 for a wild tree. Fields, houses, deer and goats leave them alone; fire or building removes them
- Why: on seed 20261114 every tall tree within reach of the hearth was gone by Y80, timber fell from ~2,000 to 0 by Y86 and 20-30 people a year died of the cold
- Visible: low cut stumps with a fan of hazel poles that grow taller until cut, a Coppice row, hover tips, timber from the coppice in History
- Watch: Hais should learn it in spring Y8 and keep ~19 stools giving 200-250 timber a year; the stool ring grows with the houses

title: Add a Families view: a family tree of every islander
body:
- New "⋔ Families" button (top left, beside Sky and History) opens a tree of every line on the island: each settler couple and their children, grandchildren and so on, with partners beside each name, ages for the living and year and age of death for the dead
- Living names are links: click one to go back to the island and follow them. The life card gets a "family tree" link that opens the tree on that person
- SIM_VERSION 33 (w.roll): graves now keep the partner (g.pt), and a grave that sinks when the burying ground is full, or an islander who sails to the far isle, is written to a roll of names so old ancestors stay in the tree. Nothing in the step path reads it, so behaviour is unchanged
- The Sky, History and Families buttons now sit in one row so the life card no longer covers the History button
- Watch: Hais has 17 living in about 8 lines; the first third generation should appear when Wenra (born Y2) has children

title: Add hawthorn hedges that turn the boars for good
body:
- SIM_VERSION 34 (w.hedge, f.hg, fauna.br; HEDGE_* in sim.js; tech 'hedges'; task kind 'hedge'; yearly `hedges`/`hedgesNew`): after 5 fences are shouldered through, the eldest sees that boars never go through the hawthorn thickets
- In autumn and winter (not in snow, storm, frost or fog) idle adults set thorn slips along every field by the woods. No timber cost. A hedge holds nothing for 3 years, then turns 97% of boars, keeps goats out of the grain, never rots and ignores storms. Fences are not rebuilt behind grown hedges. Fire kills a hedge
- Visible: bare slips, then small bushes, then a dark wall of thorn with white blossom in late spring, red haws in autumn and bare stems in winter; hover tip, Fields row shows hedged/grown, History line
- Watch: Hais should learn it in spring Y9, plant ~29 hedges that autumn, and see boar raid nights fall from 5-9 a year to 0-1 from Y12-13

title: Add stranded whales that storms wash onto the beach
body:
- SIM_VERSION 35 (w.whale {n, g, last, cur {x, y, dx, dy, at, d, m, m0, g, hands, nm, rot}, bones [{x, y, dx, dy, t, g, n}]}; tech 'whale'; task kind 'whale', keys w0..w7; WHALE_* in sim.js; yearly `whales`)
- When a storm spell ends (from Y2, at most one every 3 years), 2% per storm day (max 10%) that a whale lies on a sand tile within 26 tiles of the hearth. Up to 8 idle adults cut it, after harvest and sowing and before everything else: 18-27 meat per 3-hour spell, plus 0.08 timber of blubber per meat
- From day 3 it rots (30% of what is left lost each day); the ribs stay on the beach for good (last 6 kept). About 700-950 of 1200 meat is cut
- Visible: a grey whale half in the surf, red flesh and white ribs showing as it is cut, a green tinge once it turns, a crowd of gulls over it, skeletons that grey with age, hover tips, a Whales row in the panel
- Watch: on the live world the first whale comes around Y8-12 and then one every 4-7 years; the first stranding becomes winter tale material

title: Add late spring frosts that kill the young grain
body:
- SIM_VERSION 36 (w.frost {n, k, y, last}; f.fr; w.wx.fk/fn; FROST_* in sim.js; tech 'frost'; yearly `frosted`): from Y2, from the third day of a spring cold snap, each frost night kills a sown field with shoots under 35% grown (20%) or burns back taller grain by 10% (20%)
- Killed fields go back to fallow and are not sown again while the cold holds; once it lifts they are resown, so the harvest comes later and smaller. The first frost is a chronicle entry; big ones (8+ fields or a quarter of all) too
- Visible: rows of black, bent shoots with white rime while it is cold, a hover tip, a Frost row in the panel and a History line
- Watch: on Hais about one spring in two loses some grain, and a bad one every 3-5 years; harvest dips (e.g. 11k to 5k) but the stores carry it. Late-game growth is a little slower

title: Add children paddling in the summer shallows
body:
- SIM_VERSION 37 (w.wade {b, n, c, g, y, nm, at, s, sy, sn}; WADE_* in sim.js; tech 'wading'; task kind 'wade'; yearly `cockles`): on the first summer heatwave with 2+ children, they find the beach nearest the hearth
- From then on, on summer afternoons (10:00-18:00), 2 of 3 children go down on heat days and 1 of 3 on clear days. They paddle and dig cockles: 1-3 food a spell from a bed of 60 that refills by 2 a day
- At most once every 3 summers the sea pulls a child out and the nearest adult goes in after them. Nobody drowns. The first time is a chronicle entry
- Visible: children knee-deep off the sand with foam round their legs, throwing water at each other or bent over a cockle; hover text, a Shallows row in the panel, a History line
- Watch: Hais should learn it on the first heatwave of summer Y8, with 5-10 children in the water on hot days and 40-90 cockles a year

title: Add smudge fires that keep late frost off the grain
body:
- SIM_VERSION 38 (w.smudge {n, f, s, y, nm, at, on [{x, y, id}], last, k}; tech 'smudge'; task kind 'smudge'; SMUDGE_* in sim.js; yearly `smudged`): learned once a second late frost has killed young grain
- From the second evening of a spring cold snap, up to 12 able adults go out at 20:00 and tend smoky straw fires among the young fields (0.5 timber each a night). Each fire covers the fields within ~3 tiles, nearest the hearth first; under the smoke 80% of kills and nips are stopped. Smudgers sleep until 10:00 and wolves leave them alone
- Visible: small smouldering heaps with pale smoke drifting over the rows and a red glow at night, hover text, a Smudge row in the panel, a History line
- Watch: on Hais the first frost is due around Y9 and smudging around Y10; about half of the fields a frost would kill are saved. A small village cannot cover all its fields, so big frosts still bite

title: Add the moon: raiders row in only on dark nights
body:
- SIM_VERSION 39 (w.moon {s, nm, at}; moonAge/moonLight/moonDark/moonName and MOON_* in sim.js; tech 'moon'): a 30-day moon, 12 a year, worked out from the day number alone
- The far isle's dugout now comes only on dark-moon nights (13 of 30) or in fog. RAID_NIGHT goes from 0.03 to 0.05 on those nights, so raids are about as common as before
- Moon lore: once the watch has sat up 20 nights, at the next full moon of raid season the watcher sees the pattern. From then on the beach fire is lit only on dark or foggy nights, which saves timber and sleep
- Visible: a pixel moon with its phase in the night sky, lighter moonlit nights, silver glints on the sea, the phase in the top line after dusk, a Moon row in the panel
- Watch: Hais learns moon lore at the full moon around Y7 autumn day 76. About 8 bright nights a season go unwatched

title: Add grain rust that spreads between fields in wet summers
body:
- SIM_VERSION 40 (w.rust {n, k, g, y, yr, last, cur}; f.ru spotted tick, f.rl share lost; RUST_* in sim.js; tech 'rust'; yearly `rusted`): from Y3, after 3+ days of rain or fog between mid-spring and the end of summer, rust can come up on one growing field (at most once a year)
- Wet and windy days spread it to the fields beside it (4 sides) and each wet day takes up to 3% of a rusted field's yield, at most 60%. Heat stops it; harvest or the autumn frost ends it. Packed blocks of fields lose the most
- Visible: orange flecks on rusted grain that thicken as it spreads, hover text, a Rust row in the panel, a History line
- Test seeds: ~35 outbreaks a century, most 1-20 fields, a big one (40-125 fields, 4-9k grain) every decade or so late game. Nothing stops it yet
- Watch: Hais can see its first rust in the wet springs of Y8-9; expect a few hundred grain lost, more as the fields grow together

title: Add rogueing: pull rusted plants before rust spreads
body:
- SIM_VERSION 41 (w.rogue {n, y, k, nm, at, told}; f.rg; ROGUE_* in sim.js; tech 'rogue'; task kind 'rogue', key r<fieldId>; yearly `rogued`): learned when a rust outbreak has reached 6+ fields. The healer teaches it (sick grain is kept apart like the fevered), or the eldest if there is no healer
- 2 days after a field is spotted, idle adults walk its rows and pull the spotted plants (3 hours, 8% of the field's yield). A pulled field loses no more to rust and does not pass it on. When every spotted field still standing is pulled, the outbreak ends
- Visible: gaps in the rows and a heap of pulled grain at the edge of the field, smoking for a day; hover text, a Rogueing row in the panel, a History line
- Test seeds learn it in Y3-7; after that most outbreaks stop at 1-14 fields. Seed 4242 lost 2.3k grain to rust in 100 years
- Watch: Hais should learn it after a 10-field outbreak around Y15, with Seran teaching it, then stop most outbreaks within a few fields

title: Add bees: log hives, honey, swarms and midsummer mead
body:
- SIM_VERSION 42 (w.bees {h [{x, y, c comb, a alive, s}], hy honey, g, y, sw, sl, d, kp, m, mw}; BEE_*/MEAD_PAIR/HONEY_WOUND in sim.js; tech 'bees'; task 'honey', key e<hive>; yearly `honey`, `hives`): from Y3, on a warm summer day, a woodcutter finds a wild swarm in a hollow oak and the log is stood up by the houses
- Hives fill comb on flower days and eat it the rest of the year. Crowded hives swarm in late spring and are shaken into new logs, up to 2 + pop/8 (max 8). Honey is taken in late summer. A hive that runs out of comb in a long winter dies, and after each loss the takers leave more comb
- Honey turns to mead at the next midsummer (more couples pledge, 0.6 instead of 0.4) and goes on the healer's dressings (wounds close 2 days sooner)
- Visible: pixel log hives with a capstone, bees going out to the flowers on warm days, smoke and angry bees at the honey taking, hover text, a Bees row in the panel, a History line
- Watch: Hais should find its bees in summer Y8, have mead at the Y10 midsummer, and catch its first swarm around Y11

title: Add a lone wolf that stalks the fields by day
body:
- SIM_VERSION 43 (w.lone {n, y, dead, gone, yh, cur {id, nm, at, t, g, b, k, h}, last}; LONE_* in sim.js; beast kind 'lone'; tech 'lone'; yearly `lone`): once hunters have taken 3+ wolves and the pack is held at two, a named wolf driven from the den may turn up in spring (half the time, at most once every 8 years)
- It lies up in a thicket 10-20 tiles from the hearth and walks the treeline from 6:00 to 19:00, when the pack sleeps. It springs on anyone working alone and takes straying goats, then lies low for 5 days
- Once it has drawn blood, every hunt goes after it instead of the den (10% a hunt for a pair, and it can turn on the hunters), so the pack can grow meanwhile. If nobody kills it, it leaves after 3 years
- Visible: a bigger, paler wolf sprite that sits up to watch the village, named hover text, a Lone wolf row in the panel, a History line
- Watch: Hais should meet One-Ear in spring Y9; test seeds see 4-7 lone wolves a century, each lasting from a season to two years

title: Add rainbows after rain that the children run to find
body:
- SIM_VERSION 44 (w.bow {n, y, nm, at, c, k}, w.wx.bow {a, b, d, x, y, r}; bowComes/bowOn/bowTask/bowDone, BOW_* in sim.js; task 'bow'; yearly `bows`): when 3+ days of rain or storm break into a clear day (spring to autumn), 3 in 10 times a rainbow stands for 3 hours, in the west at 07:00 or the east at 15:00
- Two of every three children at play run to the spot where its foot comes down; the first to arrive is logged (wet grass, a puddle, it moved on). The first rainbow is a milestone
- Visible: a 7-band pixel arc over the island that fades in and out and thins towards its feet, a top-line note, a Rainbows row in the panel, hover text, a History line
- Watch: Hais should see its first rainbow in spring Y8 and about 2-3 a year after that

title: Add sky lore: the eldest calls storms a day ahead
body:
- SIM_VERSION 45 (w.lore, b.tie, w.wx.nx; LORE_* in sim.js; tech 'lore'; tasks 'tie' and firelight harvest; yearly `held`): after a storm that tears a roof, once the island has seen 100 storm days, the eldest (30+) learns to read the dusk sky
- Once it is learned, tomorrow's weather is rolled a day early. At 19:00 the reader calls about 80% of coming storms, plus a false alarm on 2.5% of evenings before rain or fog. On a warned evening adults work until 23:00: they cut ripe grain by firelight, then throw stone-weighted ropes over every roof. A roped roof holds 85% of the gusts that would tear it
- Visible: ropes and hanging stones on the thatch from the warned evening until the storm passes, a red note in the top line, a Sky lore row in the panel (calls right/missed, false alarms, roofs held), new hover text and work animation, a History line
- Watch: Hais should learn it at the next storm that tears a roof (probe: summer Y8) and then save about 1-3 roofs a year. Look for the children laughing at the stones after a false alarm

title: Add muck: goat dung forked over the fields for bigger harvests
body:
- SIM_VERSION 46 (w.muck {h heap, n, y, g, yg, nm, at}; f.mk; MUCK_* in sim.js; tech 'muck'; task 'muck', key m<fieldId>; yearly `mucked`, `muckGrain`): learned at the harvest of a field within 6 tiles of the goat pen, once goats have been kept 2 years
- A heap by the pen grows by 1 a day per goat plus 0.2 per islander (ash and scraps), up to 40 fields' worth. Idle adults carry 100 of it out in a basket and fork it over a bare field, nearest the pen first, any season but snow and storm. A mucked field yields 30% more at its next harvest
- needFields counts the extra yield of the fields a year of muck can cover, so villages clear fewer fields per person and fell less of the wood
- Visible: a dung heap against the pen wall that grows and steams in autumn and winter, dark forkfuls on bare mucked fields, thicker darker shoots on them, a basket on the back and a fork at work, hover tips, a Muck row in the panel, a History line
- Watch: Hais should learn it at this spring's harvest (Y8), muck every field from then on and need ~37-40 fields at 25 people instead of ~50

title: Add a hard-years strip to the History chart
body:
- History now shows a strip under the population chart: one column per finished year, rows for storms, fog, fever, beasts, lost fields, lost grain and deaths
- Each cell is shaded red by how bad that year was for that row compared with the island's worst year; the hardest year overall gets a white frame
- Hover a column to read that year's troubles; click it to jump to the year in the list below
- Render only (render.js, index.html); no change to the simulation or the save
- Watch: on Hais the founding year (24 storm days, 10 boar raids) should stand out until a worse year comes

title: Add foot rot that lames the goats in wet spells
body:
- SIM_VERSION 47 (w.rot {n, k, d, y, yd, yr, last, cur {at, n, d}}; g.lm lame since, g.im sound until; ROT_* in sim.js; tech 'footrot'; yearly `lame`, `rotDied`): after 3+ days of rain, fog or storm outside winter, a pen of 6+ goats can catch foot rot (at most one outbreak a year)
- It spreads through the mud from hoof to hoof, faster on wet days and in a full pen. Lame goats stay bedded in the pen: no grazing, no milk, no kids. About 0.6% die each day (kids twice as likely); they heal once the ground dries and then stay sound for 200 days
- Visible: lame goats lie in the straw with muddied coats and flies over them, a hover line, a "lame" count on the Goats row, a History line. Nothing stops it yet
- Watch: on Hais the first outbreak is due in the wet spring of Y9, and after that one every 2 years or so, killing 1-3 goats each time. Milk and kids drop in those years

title: Add hoof paring and a sick fold against foot rot
body:
- SIM_VERSION 48 (w.pare {n, y, s, nm, at, f fold tile, wash}; g.pf; PARE_* in sim.js; tech 'paring'; task 'pare', key v<goatId>; yearly `pared`): learned when an outbreak ends once foot rot has killed 2+ goats. The grown herder, the healer or the eldest puts up a hurdle fold on a tile against the pen wall (or across a corner of the pen if there is no room)
- 2 days after a goat starts to limp, an idle adult catches it, pares the hoof (2 hours) and puts it in the fold. Folded goats pass the rot to nobody, heal at 12% a day from day 4, wet or dry, and die half as often
- Visible: a straw-floored hurdle fold with the lame goats bedded in it, a flint and bowl beside it while someone pares; hover text for the fold, goats and parers; "in the fold" and "hooves pared" on the Goats row; a History line
- Test seeds: outbreaks fall from 9-18 lame goats to 1-4, and almost none die after it is learned
- Watch: Hais should lose 2 goats in its first outbreak (wet spring Y9), with Seran teaching paring that summer; after that most outbreaks stop at 1-3 goats

title: Add wolf-skin cloaks for whoever kills a lone wolf
body:
- SIM_VERSION 49 (p.cl {nm, y, by, n}; w.cloak {n, h, g}; cloakMade/cloakPass in sim.js; tech 'cloak'; grave g.cl): the hunter whose spear kills a lone wolf wears its pelt. If they already have one, it goes to the partner on the hunt
- No wolf singles out a cloak wearer (lone() skips them). At death the cloak goes to the eldest grown child, else the partner, else into the grave
- Visible: a pelt across the shoulders with two hood ears on the sprite, coloured by wolf (Pale-Eye is near white); "wears the pelt of ..." on the islander card; "buried in the pelt of ..." on graves
- Watch: on Hais, Duten and Hamor should kill Pale-Eye this spring (Y8), and Duten will wear the first cloak. Expect it to pass to one of his children decades later

title: Speed up late-game years by about 45% with identical results
body:
- Give people, fields and buildings one fixed key order (personShape/fieldShape/buildingShape), rebuilt on every load in migrate()
- Clear keys with `= undefined` instead of `delete`: almost every villager, field and building had fallen into slow dictionary mode
- Skip repeat fence/hedge searches within an hour once one finds nothing (reset when a fence or hedge claim is given up)
- Seed 4242 Y80-83 on a loaded world: ~3.8 -> ~2.1 s per year, same world as before; fingerprint() now hashes keys in sorted order
- No change to the island itself; new probes: _speedbench, _prof/_profsum, _fastprops, _keys, _tasks

title: Add squalls that catch the dugout out on the deep water
body:
- SIM_VERSION 50 (w.squall {n, y, h, s, d, b, cur, last}; squallHour/squallBegins/squallEnds/shoreWatch, SQUALL_* in sim.js; tech 'squall'; task 'shore'; yearly `squalls`): after 5 trips, each afternoon hour at sea has a 0.2% chance of a squall, x2 on hot days, x2 in autumn, x3 the day before a storm
- The paddler turns for home at half speed; each hour it blows the dugout may roll (20%). Swimmers make for the landing at 2 tiles/h and the sea can keep them (7%/h, double for the old and young); survivors lie up 5 days and the boat is lost 3 times in 5
- Kin and up to 12 idle adults run down to the landing and stand watching; whoever is there wades out to drag the swimmer in
- Visible: a black cloud with slanting rain and white caps over the boat, the dugout pitching, a swimmer with an upturned hull, hover text, a Squalls row in the panel, squalls in the Hard-years storms row
- Watch: Hais (new dugout, Y8) should see its first squall this autumn; on the live world about 0.8 a year, a boat lost every 4-5 years, a drowning every few decades

title: Add cheese: summer milk pressed into rounds for winter
body:
- SIM_VERSION 51 (w.cheese {r rack tile, p pail, c rounds, n, y, e, ye, d, f, nm, mk, at, told}; CHEESE_* in sim.js; tech 'cheese'; task 'cheese', key zc; yearly `cheese`, `cheeseEaten`): learned on a warm summer day once goats have been kept 3 years and 4+ are in milk
- Half of each day's milk goes into the pails (up to 24) instead of the stores. An idle adult presses 8 milk into a round in 3 hours and sets it on a rack by the pen wall nearest the village (holds 60)
- On bitter winter days, or when the woodpile is bare, one round per 6 small children (under 6) and old (over 55) is shared out; that day the cold hits them at 40% of the usual risk
- Visible: a hazel-rod rack with a bark roof and rounds on two shelves, a pail waiting by it, a pail carried and curd pressed under a stone, hover text, a Cheese row in the panel, History lines
- Watch: Hais should learn it this summer (Y8) and eat its first cheese in the Y8 winter; the rack stays near full until the village grows, then runs out in long cold spells

title: Add rooks on the grain and children with clappers
body:
- SIM_VERSION 52 (w.crow {b, n, e, g, y, st, ys, s, wait, cur, up, sc, nm, k}; crowHour/crowEat/crowScare/crowYear, CROW_* in sim.js; techs 'crows' and 'scaring'; task 'scare'; yearly `rooks`, `scared`): once there are 10 fields, a flock of rooks comes down by day in spring and summer on new-sown seed or ripe grain
- While down it eats 0.1% of the field per bird per hour; a sown field that loses 35% of its seed goes back to fallow and must be sown again. The flock starts at 8 and grows by 5 a year (up to 8 + fields/2, max 40)
- After 2 fields' worth is eaten, the eldest makes a clapper: idle children aged 6-13 run to the flock and mostly put it up (80% an hour once there); 40+ scarings in a year send a quarter of the flock away
- Visible: black rooks pecking in the rows, gliding in and scattering up, children with clappers over their heads, hover text, a Rooks row in the panel, rooks in History and in the Hard-years grain row. Sowing now clears old crop losses on a field
- Watch: Hais should get its first flock this summer (Y8) and the clappers next spring; expect 150-1100 grain a year to rooks and the flock to rise and fall between ~14 and 40

title: Add a good-years strip to the History chart
body:
- History now shows a green strip under the red hard-years strip: rows for births, harvest, sea, hunt, larder and play
- Brighter green is a bigger year for that row; the best year overall gets a white frame, and the caption names it
- Hover a column to read the year, click it to jump to that year in the list (its title turns green)
- Both strips share one drawing function and the same label width, so their year columns line up
- Render only: no change to the simulation or the saved world

title: Add fog signs: the sky reader calls fog and the goats stay in
body:
- SIM_VERSION 53 (w.lore gains fl, fnm, fg, fn, fh, fm, ff, fk, fc; fogRead/fogKept/learnFog in sim.js, FOG_* constants; tech 'foglore'): learned when a fog of 2+ days lifts, once the island has sky lore, goats, and a past wolf attack or someone lost in the fog
- At the evening fire the eldest calls about 70% of coming fogs, with a rare false alarm. On a called fog day, and on every day after the first in a long fog, the goats stay shut in the pen (no wolf can take one from the grazing) and most children and old ones who would wander off stay by the houses
- Visible: "Fog by morning" evening lines, a Fog signs row (calls, misses, false alarms, days the herd was kept in), "kept in the pen out of the fog" on goat hover
- Watch: Hais should learn it at the next 2-day fog (autumn Y8, Morceem), then call 3-4 fogs a year; goats lost in fog should drop close to zero

title: Island improvements
Make the page feel live: smooth walking, work at the task, bubbles, a coming-up strip and a welcome back
body:
- People and animals glide between pixels and walk short legs at a steady pace
- Axes, sickles, seed, mallets and baskets move at the task
- Speech bubbles over whoever you follow and now and then over someone at work; the follow card keeps a diary
- Coming up: a private copy of the island is played 6 hours ahead; deaths are hidden and raids only hinted at
- While you were away: what happened since your last visit and what is new in the rules
- An open page reloads itself when the rules change

title: Add a bear that raids the bee logs and cheese rack
body:
- SIM_VERSION 55 (w.bear; beast k 'bear'; BEAR_* in sim.js; tech 'bear'; yearly `bear`): from year 5, once there is honey or cheese, a late summer may bring a named bear over the bar from the far isle; it lies up in a thicket until the first frosts (doy 282)
- On about one quiet night in eight it walks in for the heaviest bee log or the cheese rack and eats until a sleeper wakes (a dog makes it likely) and drives it off with a brand; it may split a log (the hive dies) or swipe at the one with the brand (a wound, never a death)
- Shown on the map at night (it rears up at the log), with a split-log sprite, a tooltip, a Bear row in Beasts and in the hard-years strip
- Often the same bear comes back; nothing stops it yet, so a later visit can add a hunt, raised hives or a thorn ring

title: Add seals that eat the deep fish, and sealskin floats
body:
- SIM_VERSION 56 (w.seal; techs 'seals' and 'sealing'; task 'seal'; yearly `seals`, `sealsTaken`, `sealFish`): after 40 dugout trips a herd of 5 grey seals hauls out on a quiet sand beach, eats from the dugout's deep-water fish all year and pups every early winter
- Once the seals have eaten 500 fish, a hunter goes down with a club when the pups are on the sand: meat, blubber for the fire, a skin. After each try the herd keeps off for 9 days, and it is never taken below 8
- The first skin becomes a float in the dugout once the island has seen a squall: a swimmer who holds on to it drowns about a third as often. It perishes after 5 years
- Visible: seals hauled out by day (heads lift, white pups), heads bobbing offshore at night or when someone comes near, the club, a seal carried home, the float in the dugout and in a swimmer's arms, a Seals row and tooltip
- Watch: Hais (canoe trips 249) should find its seals this spring or summer (Y11) and start sealing in the Y12 winter; expect the dugout catch to fall from ~900 to ~300-480 fish a year

title: Add a midsummer footrace with an oak wreath for the winner
body:
- SIM_VERSION 57 (w.fest.race {d, sx/sy, ex/ey, lx/ly, rs, win, nm}, rn, rl; tech 'race'; task 'race'; deed 'r', byname "the Swift" at 3 wins)
- At 17:00 on midsummer up to 8 islanders aged 9-30 line up by the bonfire, run out to a hazel stake 6-9 tiles away over open grass and back by 19:00; the winner is crowned at 20:00. The first race needs a runner under 16
- Speed comes from age, a fixed "quick legs" per islander and luck, so some win again and again. A single winner of 17+ is pledged that night 70% of the time
- Visible: the stake with a red rag, runners with pumping arms in a pale colour, a green oak wreath on the winner while the dance goes on, top-line note, a Race row under Folk
- Watch: Hais runs its first race at the Y11 midsummer (summer day 46, 4 runners); on the probe Anfen became the Swift by Y14

title: Add scarecrows that the rooks slowly see through
body:
- Fix the blank page: render.js declared `RCOL` twice (bear and rats), so the bundle did not parse; the bear palette is now `BEARCOL`, and build.mjs fails if the bundle does not parse
- SIM_VERSION 58 (w.crow gains m, mk, mt, my, mv, mo, mnm, mat; scareTurn/scareSite/scareTask/scareDone in sim.js, SCARE_* constants; tech 'scarecrow'; task 'crowman', key zk; yearly `crowTurned`): learned once the children have driven the flock off 30 times
- Idle adults stand 1 + fields/10 scarecrows (max 8, 1 timber each, a spare hide makes one last longer); a flock picking a field within ~3 tiles of one wheels away, but each turn wears it down and after 20-30 turns a rook sits on its hat and it must be moved to a new field
- Visible: scarecrows in the fields (hide or straw coat, a rook on the hat when found out), carried over the shoulder and hammered in, hover text, scarecrow counts in the Rooks row
- Watch: Hais learns it this spring (Y11); on the live world rook losses fall from ~200-400 to ~30-60 grain a year and found-out scarecrows get moved 2-3 times a year

title: Add whooping cough that sweeps through the children
body:
- SIM_VERSION 59 (w.cough {k, n, d, all, lost, y, yd, end, who, nu}; p.cg cough ends, p.cgi had it; coughDay/coughs in sim.js, COUGH_* constants; tech 'cough'; yearly `coughs`, `coughDied`)
- Settlers and newcomers had it as children elsewhere; once 7+ island-born children never have, it can take hold autumn to spring (4+ years apart) and runs through nearly all of them in a few weeks. Babies under 2 are the ones at risk
- Coughing children sit in the doorway instead of scaring rooks, wading or racing; a parent stays home with each coughing child under 4, so work is lost
- Visible: children doubled over in coughing fits on the doorsteps, a parent sat beside them, "N whooping" in the People row, cough in the History sickness row
- Watch: Hais (15 children, none have had it) should get its first outbreak in the Y11 autumn; on seed 4242 it comes every 5-9 years and takes about 2 babies each time at 100+ people

title: Add a ring of standing stones hauled up from the shore
body:
- SIM_VERSION 60 (w.stones {cx, cy, sx, sy, s[], cur, n, y, hurt, at, nm, done}; learnStones/stoneDay/stoneCrew/stoneHour/stoneUp/stoneRope, STONE_* in sim.js; tech 'stones'; task 'stone'; deed `s`): once there are 20+ islanders, 10 grown and 200 food a head, the eldest marks out a ring of 8 stakes on open grass 8-18 tiles from the hearth and picks boulders on a beach 9-20 tiles from it
- Each summer or early autumn after the harvest (from day 140, with 120 food a head and no ripe fields), up to 10 islanders aged 16-50 lever one boulder onto rollers and drag it to the ring at 0.06 tiles/h per hauler (0.6 max, half in rain or fog), then raise it over 4 h. Each stone is for one of the dead, oldest grave first, and is followed by a feast (3 food a head). Each hour on the ropes has a 0.4% chance of a crushed foot (8 days laid up)
- Visible: boulders on the shore, stakes and an open pit in the ring, the stone sliding on log rollers with hide ropes out to the haulers, a stone coming upright on a prop, grey slabs with lichen and snow caps, hover text for stones, ring and boulders, a Stones row under Folk
- Watch: Hais should mark its ring this summer (Y11, after day 140) and raise the first stone within days, then one a summer until about Y18. Each haul takes 3-5 game days and keeps most of the grown-ups away from other work
